sections.content: How many people are "programmers and software development professionals"?

264,070 people

were counted on the census as "programmers and software development professionals" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Programmers and software development professionals design, develop, test, implement and maintain software systems on a range of platforms in order to meet the specifications and business objectives of the information system.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "programmers and software development professionals" there were more men than women (84.2% compared with 15.8%).

This means "programmers and software development professionals" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "science, research, engineering and technology professionals".

Men made up 84.2% and women made up 15.8% of "programmers and software development professionals"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "programmers and software development professionals" included:

  • chartered surveyors
  • plant and machine operatives (other)
  • elementary storage supervisors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "programmers and software development professionals", 17.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "programmers and software development professionals" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "programmers and software development professionals" included:

  • graphic and multimedia designers
  • web design professionals
  • insurance underwriters

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "programmers and software development professionals" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "programmers and software development professionals" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "programmers and software development professionals", 7.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (93.1% compared with 6.9%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (91%) than self-employed (9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Tower Hamlets, this is in the same region of London.
